title: Resident Marine Mammals of Tanon Strait v. Secretary Angelo Reyes
petitioner: Resident Marine Mammals of the Protected Seascape Tanon Strait
summary: The Supreme Court recognized the legal standing of marine mammals (through their stewards) to file a case protecting their habitat against oil exploration in a protected seascape. This expanded the concept of standing in environmental cases.
doctrine: Under the Rules of Procedure for Environmental Cases, any Filipino citizen in representation of others, including minors and generations yet unborn, may file an action to enforce environmental rights. The liberal standing rule extends to environmental cases involving the protection of natural habitats.
citedStatutes: Rules of Procedure for Environmental Cases Rule 2 Sec. 4
fullText:
LEONARDO-DE CASTRO, J.:

This unusual case presents the novel question of whether marine mammals, through their human stewards, have standing to sue for the protection of their habitat.

The Rules of Procedure for Environmental Cases provide for a liberal rule on standing. Under Section 4 of Rule 2, any Filipino citizen in representation of others, including minors and generations yet unborn, may file an action. The stewardship principle allows concerned citizens to file suit on behalf of the environment and its inhabitants.

The Court recognizes that environmental cases require a more liberal approach to standing, consistent with the constitutional policy of protecting and advancing the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology.
